subject: genetics
question: **Type:** pedigree The pedigree shows an autosomal dominant disorder in which onset is progressively earlier in each successive generation. Which molecular feature explains this pattern of anticipation in Huntington disease? ```text PEDIGREE: Generation I: I-1 affected male; I-2 unaffected female, partners Generation II: II-1 unaffected female; II-2 affected male; II-3 affected female; II-4 unaffected male Generation III: III-1 affected female; III-2 affected male, children of II-2 Key inference: Both sexes are affected, every affected person has an affected parent, male to male transmission occurs, and onset is earlier in each successive generation. Most consistent mode: autosomal dominant ```

options.text: Loss of function of huntingtin caused by a frameshift mutation in the *HTT* coding sequence
CAG repeat expansion in *HTT* that tends to lengthen when transmitted, producing a gain of function and earlier onset in later generations
Deletion of the short arm of chromosome 5 that removes the *HTT* locus
A trinucleotide repeat that is inherited at an identical, fixed length in every generation

explanation: Huntington disease is caused by a CAG repeat expansion in *HTT* (4p16.3) that acts by gain of function, and the repeat tends to lengthen with transmission, so each successive generation tends to have earlier onset and more severe symptoms, which is anticipation. A frameshift mutation would cause loss of function, and D describes fixed repeat length, both incompatible with the pattern in the pedigree. C is Cri du chat syndrome, a 5p deletion, which is unrelated to repeat expansion.
